Whistleblower system

The whistleblower system lets you report any misconduct, especially violations of applicable law and
internal instructions and procedures. This service is offered to employees and external persons who
wish to draw attention to breaches of the rules at Rheinmetall companies and their suppliers and
business partners.

[ REPORT VIOLATION ][9]
Investor Relations
How can I register for the Annual General Meeting?

If you hold Rheinmetall shares, the invitation will be sent to you automatically by the custodian
bank. The invitation contains information on the time and location of the Annual General Meeting.
Details can also be found on our website at Rheinmetall / Investor Relations / Annual General
Meeting.

[ Learn more ][10]
How can I buy Rheinmetall shares?

Please contact your custodian bank, investment advisor or broker regarding trading in shares.

When and where will the next Annual General Meeting take place?

The Annual General Meeting will be held on the basis of article 15 (3) of the company's statues as a
virtual Annual General Meeting in accordance with article 118a (1) sentence 1 of the German Stock
Corporation Act (AktG), without the physical presence of shareholders or their proxies (with the
exception of the company's proxies) at the location of the Annual General Meeting. The location of
the Annual General Meeting within the meaning of the German Stock Corporation Act is Rheinmetall
Platz 1, 40476 Düsseldorf.

[ Learn more ][11]
At what point do you need to hold the share to be entitled to receive a dividend?

The share must be booked into your portfolio account of your bank on the day of the Annual General
Meeting.

When will the dividend be paid?

Pursuant to Section 58 para. 4 sentence 2 AktG, the claim to the dividend will be due on the third
business day following the resolution of the Annual General Meeting, i.e. on Friday, 15 May 2026.

Where can I find the invitation to the Annual General Meeting?

Please find the invitation to the Annual General Meeting on our website.

[ Lean more ][12]
What are the requirements for participating in the virtual AGM and when is the authentic deadline?

Shareholders who are entitled to participate in the virtual Annual General Meeting, and in
particular to exercise their voting rights, are those who are shareholders of the Company at the
close of business on the 22nd day before the Annual General Meeting, i.e. on 20 April 2026 (24:00 =
end of day CEST) (record date), and register for the Annual General Meeting in good time.

[ REGISTRATION DETAILS CAN BE FOUND IN THE ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING INVITATION ][13]

Give aways / advertising material / merchandise

Where can I order Rheinmetall advertising material/merchandise?

Thank you for your interest in Rheinmetall promotional merchandise.
Currently, we do not operate an online shop, but we are working on a concept.

As soon as it is possible to order Rheinmetall items via our website, we will publish this.

Career

How can I apply for a job at Rheinmetall?

Thank you for your interest in Rheinmetall.

Please send us your application documents via the job gateway on our website. Unfortunately, we
cannot accept or process applications by email due to data protection regulations.

[ Learn more ][5]
Do you have questions about your application or the application process?
[ Contact us ][6]
I am a student at a university / higher education institution and am interested in Rheinmetall.

Are you interested in Rheinmetall as part of your student research project?

You can contact us here regarding the following:
1. Supervision of seminar papers
2. Company surveys
3. Expert interviews

Please do not forward enquiries from the university to the press office, as they can only accept
enquiries from media representatives.

If you are interested in the many career opportunities at Rheinmetall, you will find information on
the wide range of entry options under ‘Career’.

[ Contact us ][7]
I am organising career/job fairs and events, and would like to get in touch with Rheinmetall.

University Marketing

[ Contact us ][8]

Whistleblower system (report violation)

Whistleblower system

The whistleblower system lets you report any misconduct, especially violations of applicable law and
internal instructions and procedures. This service is offered to employees and external persons who
wish to draw attention to breaches of the rules at Rheinmetall companies and their suppliers and
business partners.

[ REPORT VIOLATION ][9]
Investor Relations
How can I register for the Annual General Meeting?

If you hold Rheinmetall shares, the invitation will be sent to you automatically by the custodian
bank. The invitation contains information on the time and location of the Annual General Meeting.
Details can also be found on our website at Rheinmetall / Investor Relations / Annual General
Meeting.

[ Learn more ][10]
How can I buy Rheinmetall shares?

Please contact your custodian bank, investment advisor or broker regarding trading in shares.

When and where will the next Annual General Meeting take place?

The Annual General Meeting will be held on the basis of article 15 (3) of the company's statues as a
virtual Annual General Meeting in accordance with article 118a (1) sentence 1 of the German Stock
Corporation Act (AktG), without the physical presence of shareholders or their proxies (with the
exception of the company's proxies) at the location of the Annual General Meeting. The location of
the Annual General Meeting within the meaning of the German Stock Corporation Act is Rheinmetall
Platz 1, 40476 Düsseldorf.

[ Learn more ][11]
At what point do you need to hold the share to be entitled to receive a dividend?

The share must be booked into your portfolio account of your bank on the day of the Annual General
Meeting.

When will the dividend be paid?

Pursuant to Section 58 para. 4 sentence 2 AktG, the claim to the dividend will be due on the third
business day following the resolution of the Annual General Meeting, i.e. on Friday, 15 May 2026.

Where can I find the invitation to the Annual General Meeting?

Please find the invitation to the Annual General Meeting on our website.

[ Lean more ][12]
What are the requirements for participating in the virtual AGM and when is the authentic deadline?

Shareholders who are entitled to participate in the virtual Annual General Meeting, and in
particular to exercise their voting rights, are those who are shareholders of the Company at the
close of business on the 22nd day before the Annual General Meeting, i.e. on 20 April 2026 (24:00 =
end of day CEST) (record date), and register for the Annual General Meeting in good time.

[ REGISTRATION DETAILS CAN BE FOUND IN THE ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING INVITATION ][13]

Press and Public Relations

I am a media representative and would like to contact Rheinmetall with an editorial enquiry.

Are you a representative of the media/press and would like to submit a press enquiry?

Please use our press portal for this.

[ Lean more ][14]
As a media representative, I am interested in a filming date or a visit to one of Rheinmetall's
sites.

As much as we appreciate your interest in Rheinmetall, we must point out that we are currently
receiving a very high amount of media enquiries regarding the topic of the “boom in defence industry
orders”, particularly those involving requests for site visits.

Unfortunately, due to capacity constraints, we are unable to accommodate the large number of visit
requests—especially given the strict security regulations in place at our sites.

We kindly ask for your understanding.

Site visits

I am interested in visiting Rheinmetall as a private person.

Due to high security restrictions, we are unfortunately unable to offer visits or site tours for
interested groups or private persons. Our sites are not open to the public.

reliability in the quality of our products and customer service, often taking unconventional and

## Use of Content (Including AI Systems)

Use of content from this site must include attribution to RP Photonics, with a link to the used
page. Reproduction or repackaging of substantial parts without proper attribution is not permitted.

This explicitly holds also for AI-generated outputs (e.g., by large language models or
conversational agents).

## Mass Mails and Fraudulent Mails from RP Photonics?

Occasionally, large amounts of spam (unwanted mass mails), phishing attempts and similar kinds of
fraudulent mails are spread which are falsely claiming an e-mail address in the domain
`rp-photonics.com` as the sender, sometimes even the sender address of the managing director. Some
of those mails have attachments containing malware, and others try to make you click on a dubious
link. Obviously, behind such activities there are **criminals who try to gain trust from possible
victims by pretending that their mails are from RP Photonics, a reputable source**. Some of them are
also abusing our company logo and further data, e.g. our telephone number.

Note that such fraudulent mails are **never** sent through our mail server. Instead, criminals use
their own mail server, on which we have no control whatsoever, and simply claim our domain to be the
sender ([e-mail spoofing][24]). Unfortunately, the basic e-mail standards allow that without any
checks. (By the way, our servers have so far never been hacked; we protect them very carefully.)
However, there are several mechanisms which allow receiving mail servers to check for such abuse:
* An [**SPF record**][25], published through our domain (in the domain name system DNS), indicates
that legitimate mails from RP Photonics are all sent through a server of our hoster. In other
words, mails coming from other mail servers are all illegitimate, not from us.
* Since October 2023, all our mails are digitally signed with [**DKIM**][26]. That certificate, when
properly validated, proves (a) that the mails are from our server and (b) that they have not been
modified on the way. In other words, any mails without a valid DKIM certificate cannot be from us.
* Further, we have published a [**DMARC** record][27], instructing receiving mail servers to
strictly check SPF and DKIM, and reject all mails not passing both tests.

## Mass Mails and Fraudulent Mails from RP Photonics?

Occasionally, large amounts of spam (unwanted mass mails), phishing attempts and similar kinds of
fraudulent mails are spread which are falsely claiming an e-mail address in the domain
`rp-photonics.com` as the sender, sometimes even the sender address of the managing director. Some
of those mails have attachments containing malware, and others try to make you click on a dubious
link. Obviously, behind such activities there are **criminals who try to gain trust from possible
victims by pretending that their mails are from RP Photonics, a reputable source**. Some of them are
also abusing our company logo and further data, e.g. our telephone number.

Note that such fraudulent mails are **never** sent through our mail server. Instead, criminals use
their own mail server, on which we have no control whatsoever, and simply claim our domain to be the
sender ([e-mail spoofing][24]). Unfortunately, the basic e-mail standards allow that without any
checks. (By the way, our servers have so far never been hacked; we protect them very carefully.)
However, there are several mechanisms which allow receiving mail servers to check for such abuse:
* An [**SPF record**][25], published through our domain (in the domain name system DNS), indicates
that legitimate mails from RP Photonics are all sent through a server of our hoster. In other
words, mails coming from other mail servers are all illegitimate, not from us.
* Since October 2023, all our mails are digitally signed with [**DKIM**][26]. That certificate, when
properly validated, proves (a) that the mails are from our server and (b) that they have not been
modified on the way. In other words, any mails without a valid DKIM certificate cannot be from us.
* Further, we have published a [**DMARC** record][27], instructing receiving mail servers to
strictly check SPF and DKIM, and reject all mails not passing both tests.

Therefore, you should no longer receive illegitimate mails abusing our domain, *provided that your
mail server is properly set up to make the mentioned tests*. For any reasonable provider, that
should be the case.

For the case that anything dubious still gets through, we can give some indications for checking
whether such mails are from us:
* Our mails are all properly formatted, written with decent language etc.; the style is usually very
different from what spammers typically use. Fortunately, spammers normally invest very little time
into optimizing such mails; they are mostly targeting easy victims, who do not critically check
what to accept. However, that might soon change since fraudsters are starting to use artificial
intelligence.
* Of course, RP Photonics is never sending out mails concerning items which are totally unrelated to
its business. However, some abuse has also happened in the context of photonics.
* All our mails strictly come from the domain **rp-photonics.com** only, never e.g. from Gmail.
* Messages from [Dr. Paschotta][28], the founder and managing director of RP Photonics (but not our
[newsletter][29] mailings) are always **digitally signed**; the S/MIME signature can be validated
by your e-mail program and then confirms that a mail is really from the claimed sender.
* RP Photonics may occasionally ask you to click on a link in our domain (rp-photonics.com), e.g. to
view one of our web pages such as an Encyclopedia or blog article, but not on dubious other
domains.
* In case of doubt, just forward such an alleged RP Photonics message to us, and we will tell you
whether it was from us.

**Please do *not* put our addresses or our domain on any e-mail blacklist.** Indeed, you should be
safe putting them on any e-mail whitelist, assuming that your mail server properly does the usual
tests.

# Dr. Rüdiger Paschotta, Founder and Managing Director of RP Photonics AG

[Picture of Dr. Rüdiger Paschotta]

Dr. Rüdiger Paschotta has an international reputation as a highly distinguished expert in technical
areas such as lasers and amplifiers, nonlinear optics, fiber technology, ultrashort pulses, and
noise in optics. He is author or coauthor of many [publications][15], in particular of over 100
articles in scientific journals, over 120 presentations at international conferences, and of several
books and book chapters. Also, he is the author of the well-known [RP Photonics Encyclopedia][16],
an extremely popular authoritative resource.

Dr. Paschotta originally started his career in scientific research. In 2002, he achieved the
habilitation at ETH Zürich and received the [Fresnel Prize of the European Physical Society
(EPS)][17] in 2002. Despite his success as a researcher (see his [CV with publication list][18]), in
2004 he started the company RP Photonics Consulting GmbH in Zürich, Switzerland. (The company moved
to Bad Dürrheim, Germany, in 2010, and [to Frauenfeld, Switzerland, in 2022][19], and is now RP
Photonics AG.) He [serves][20] companies in the photonics industry worldwide. Typical tasks are to
work out feasibility studies and designs for lasers and other photonic devices, to identify and
solve technical problems, to find suitable laser sources for specific applications, and to do
[tailored staff training courses][21] on specialized subjects. Dr. Paschotta regularly achieves very
high levels of customer satisfaction.

He is also a thought leader and influencer in photonics. For example:
* He is a strong advocate of [simulation in photonics][22] as a powerful method for understanding
technology and achieving improvements — not only with higher quality results, but also with higher
efficiency.
* He warmly recommends investing more in education, the key for future success. He very actively
contributes to photonics education worldwide — in particular, with his open-access [RP Photonics
Encyclopedia][23], but also with [tailored training courses][24].
* He firmly stands for reliable truth and for scientific methods as the best way to establish it. In
particular, government actions should always be based on evidence rather than ideology. Science
and engineering people should firmly stand up against attacks on science and reason.
* He is fully aware that cooperation is key for success. That must include international cooperation
in many fields, such as science, climate crisis and trade.

Besides, Dr. Paschotta has become an expert in [digital marketing][25] of photonics products. He has
developed the [RP Photonics Buyer's Guide][26] and established it as the premier resource for
finding photonics suppliers.

## Research Experience
* 01/1992 to 09/1994: doctorate at the [University of Konstanz][39], Germany, in the group of Prof.
J. Mlynek. Obtained the Ph. D. degree with "summa cum laude" (highest distinction) for work in
quantum optics (squeezed light) and nonlinear optics.
* 10/1994 to 01/1997: post-doc in the [Optoelectronics Research Centre][40], Southampton, UK, with
Prof. A. C. Tropper and Prof. D. C. Hanna, working on fiber lasers, upconversion lasers, laser
spectroscopy, laser modeling and simulation, ultrashort pulse generation. After that period, a
fruitful research collaboration was continued for many years with the mentioned persons and others
in the institution.
* 02/1997 to 10/1997: post-doc at the [University of Paderborn][41] (Germany), with Prof. W. Sohler,
working on quasi-phase-matched integrated nonlinear optical devices.
* 11/1997 to 06/2005: leader of a research group in the Institute of Quantum Electronics, [ETH
Zurich][42], within the group of U. Keller, working on all-solid-state picosecond and femtosecond
lasers, mode-locked high-power lasers, mode-locked semiconductor lasers (VECSELs), nonlinear
frequency conversion of ultrashort pulses, laser noise, computer modeling in laser physics and
nonlinear optics.
In her official report of Jan. 2002, concerning R. Paschotta's habilitation, Prof. Keller wrote:
“I consider him as the best scientist in this field within his peer group worldwide and he has
been my best post-doc I have had so far. Presently, he is in charge of eight graduate students in
my group and everybody is speaking very highly of him and enjoys working with him.”
* Since 07/2005: further scientific work (not related to ETH Zurich) while working as a technical
consultant (see below).

# About RPMC

### As your trusted OEM laser partner, RPMC Lasers simplifies your journey by reducing stress,
### saving time, and guiding you to the ideal laser solution for your next project.

**Our skilled team of product and account managers are dedicated to helping you find the perfect
laser for any application – backed by nearly three decades of experience and strong ties with
top-tier manufacturers.**

### Our Expertise:
* 29+ years of industry knowledge, providing expert advice and reliable support
* In-depth knowledge of diode lasers, CW and pulsed lasers, and laser amplifiers
* Long-term partnerships with industry-leading laser manufacturers
* Custom application-driven solutions tailored to your specific needs
* Extensive experience with Medical and Defense industry certifications

#### Let Us Help Find Your Solution Today!

[ Get Started Now!][71]

RPMC Lasers is your strategic partner and trusted source for high-quality laser solutions. Whether
you require off-the-shelf lasers, fully customized designs, or expert technical guidance, we offer
the expertise, reliability, and support necessary to ensure you find the right laser at the right
price.

### What We Offer:
* A small-team approach, delivering personalized attention, fast & honest answers
* A single point of contact for a streamlined experience
* Access to 10,000+ standard laser diodes and solid-state lasers
* 100+ laser options in stock and ready to ship
* U.S.-made solutions for many applications, avoiding tariffs & international shipping issues
* Just-in-time delivery options and buffer stock management
* High-Capacity Manufacturing for large-scale projects
* Direct collaboration with the manufacturer’s engineering team to tackle your toughest challenges
* Ensures alignment, efficiency, and a focus on your success
* Access to the manufacturer’s application lab and demo units, when available

the situation. The first question you should ask yourself when considering which type of laser to

## Pulsed Lasers FAQs

What is a Pulsed Laser?
**What is a Pulsed Laser?**

A [pulsed laser][121] is any laser that does not emit a continuous-wave (CW) laser beam. Instead,
they emit light pulses at some duration with some period of ‘off’ time between pulses and a
frequency measured in cycles per second (Hz). There are several different methods for pulse
generation, including passive and active q-switching and mode-locking. Pulsed lasers store energy
and release it in these pulses or energy packets. This pulsing can be very beneficial, for example,
when machining certain materials or features. The pulse can rapidly deliver the stored energy, with
downtime in between, preventing too much heat from building up in the material. If you would like to
read more about q-switches and the pros and cons of passive vs active q-switches, check out this
blog “[The Advantages and Disadvantages of Passive vs Active Q-Switching][122],” or check out our
[Overview of Pulsed Lasers][123] section on our Lasers 101 Page!

What is the best laser for LIDAR?
**What is the best laser for LIDAR?**

There are actually numerous laser types that work well for various [LIDAR][124] and [3D
Scanning][125] applications. The answer comes down to what you want to measure or map. If your
target is stationary, and distance is the only necessary measurement, short-pulsed lasers, with
pulse durations of a few nanoseconds (even <1ns) and high pulse energy are what you’re looking for.
This is also accurate for 3D scanning applications (given a stationary, albeit a much closer
target), but select applications can also benefit from frequency-modulated, single-frequency
(narrow-linewidth) fiber lasers. If your target is moving, and speed is the critical measurement,
you need a single-frequency laser to ensure accurate measurement of the Doppler shift. If you want
to learn more about the various forms of LIDAR and the critical laser source requirements, check out
our [LIDAR][126] page for a list of detailed articles, as well as all the LIDAR laser source
products we offer. Get more information from our Lasers 101, Blogs, Whitepapers, FAQs, and Press
Release pages in our [Knowledge Center][127]!

## Component FAQs

Can I operate multiple laser diodes from the same power supply?
**Can I operate multiple laser diodes from the same power supply?**

The same power supply can drive multiple [laser diodes][124] if they are connected in series, but
they must never be connected in parallel. When two diodes are connected in series, they will
function properly as long as the compliance voltage is large enough to cover the voltage drop across
each diode. For example, suppose you are trying to power two diode lasers, each with an operating
voltage of 1.9 V, and connect the two in series. In that case, the pulsed or CW laser driver must
have a total voltage capacity greater than 3.8 V. This configuration works because diodes share the
same current when connected in series. In contrast, when two diodes are connected in parallel, the
current is no longer shared between the two diodes. Get more details on the topic in this article:

## CW Lasers FAQs

How do I align my optical system?
**How do I align my optical system?**

Laser alignment can be a challenging task, but aligning a laser beam doesn’t have to be as
complicated as it might seem with the right optical alignment tools and proper laser alignment
techniques. Multiple optical alignment techniques have been developed over the years, utilized by
technicians and engineers to simplify the alignment process. With the development of these universal
laser beam alignment methods, along with some laser alignment tips and tricks, you don’t need to be
a laser expert to perform your alignments with relative ease, ensuring your laser beam path is right
where you want it to be and your beam is on target every time. Read our article, titled “[Laser
Alignment: HeNe Lasers, Methods, and Helpful Tips][128]” to get the knowledge and advice you need
for proper optical beam path alignment utilizing [HeNe Lasers][129]. Get more information from our
Lasers 101, Blogs, Whitepapers, FAQs, and Press Release pages in our [Knowledge Center][130]!

Should I choose multimode or single-mode for Raman spectroscopy?
**Should I choose multimode or single-mode for Raman spectroscopy?**

On the surface, this seems like a simple question since [Raman][131] is a nonlinear optical effect
and therefore the tighter the beam can be focused the higher the conversion efficiency. Seemingly a
single-mode laser would be preferable, but in practice there are other factors that can complicate
the situation. The first question you should ask yourself when considering which type of laser to
choose is whether you are doing microscopy or bulk sampling. If the answer to that question is
microscopy, then you immediately should go with a single mode laser. Since the goal of any
microscopy system is to produce the highest resolution image possible, the number one consideration
should be how tightly can the laser beam be focused down. However, there are several other
considerations when choosing between multimode and single-mode. Learn which is best for you in this
article: “[Multimode vs Single-Mode Lasers for Raman Spectroscopy][132].” Get more information from
our Lasers 101, Blogs, Whitepapers, FAQs, and Press Release pages in our [Knowledge Center][133]!

The neoMOS ultrashort pulse laser series is a reliable, low-maintenance system designed for 24/7
industrial use. The ultra-compact laser head has the smallest footprint available and can be
customized for a range of laser parameters, allowing easy integration and flexibility with various
demanding processing applications, including glasses and plastics. It offers pulse widths from 700fs
to 70ps, repetition rates from single-shot to 80MHz, up to 500µJ pulse energy, average output powers
up to 100W, multi-megawatt peak powers, and perfect TEM00 beam quality @ 1064nm.

### Benefits:
* **Reliable and low-maintenance system:** Customers can rely on the neoMOS laser series to work
consistently and efficiently with minimal upkeep required, which can save time and money on
maintenance and repair costs.
* **Small footprint for easy integration:** The compact size of the laser head makes it easy to
integrate into different systems, which can save space and enable more versatile applications.
* **High stability and long lifetime:** The neoMOS laser series is designed for 24/7 industrial use
with high stability and long service life, which can provide peace of mind and minimize downtime.
* **Flexible and customizable:** Customers can customize the neoMOS laser system to meet specific
needs and requirements, providing a wide range of laser parameters and pulse durations. This
flexibility can allow for more precise and effective processing.
* **Suitable for processing demanding materials:** The multi-megawatt level peak-power and ultrafast
pulses make it suitable for processing even the most demanding materials, including transparent
glasses and plastics. This capability can enable new applications and improve efficiency in
existing ones.
* **MOPA architecture for various laser parameters and pulse durations:** The MOPA architecture of
the neoMOS laser series combines amplifier modules with different oscillators, allowing for
various laser parameters and pulse durations from the same laser platform. This versatility can
provide more options and tailored performance.
* **Variable pulse durations and repetition rates:** Continuous-wave laser modulation to achieve
variable pulse durations and repetition rates, enabling the generation of low-noise pulsed
single-frequency systems. This capability can allow for more precise and controlled processing.
* **Excellent TEM00 beam quality:** All neoMOS laser systems have a nice Gaussian beam with good
beam quality, which can provide more accurate and consistent processing results.

The multi-megawatt level peak-power and ultrafast pulses make the neoMOS series suitable for
processing even the most demanding materials, including transparent glasses and plastics. Its
typical applications include photovoltaic and electronics production, display glass processing, as
well as security and decorative marking.

The neoMOS laser series has a MOPA architecture that combines amplifier modules with different
oscillators, allowing the addressing of various laser parameters and pulse durations from the same
laser platform. Different seed laser technologies are available for the pulse duration range of a
few nanoseconds down to about 100 fs, such as active (AQS) and passive q-switched (PQS) oscillators,
modulated laser diodes (LD), or pulse-picked mode-locked oscillators (ML).

The neoMOS laser series offers continuous wave laser modulation to achieve variable pulse durations
and repetition rates, enabling the generation of low-noise pulsed single-frequency systems. The
laser system has been demonstrated to achieve energy levels greater than 40 mJ or greater than 200 W
average power. The system comes equipped with standard neoCON software that allows users to set all
relevant laser parameters and monitor system control signals and temperatures.

If you have any questions or need more information, please contact us.

### neoMOS “SMAART”:

The SMAART combination of pico- and femtosecond laser pulses within one compact laser system. The
alliance is based on high reliable and low maintenance fiber oscillators and robust solid-state
amplifiers. The newly developed laser system further expands the neoMOS pulse duration range into
the are of less than 900fs up to a few tens of picoseconds, or even nanoseconds.
* **Pulse durations:** 40ps / 900fs
* **Output Power:** 100W / 75W
* **Pulse Energy:** Up to 500µJ / 400µJ
* **Repetition Rates:** 200kHz to 2MHz
* **Beam Quality:** TEM00 / M² < 1.3

### neoMOS 700fs:

This femtosecond laser series combines the reliability and low maintenance of a state of the art
fiber oscillator with a solid-state amplifier. The newly developed laser system further expands the
neoMOS pulse duration range into the area of less than 700fs. The CPA free technology allows for
bandwidth limited pulses in the smallest footprint available.
* **Pulse duration:** < 700fs
* **Output Power:** 100W
* **Pulse Energy:** Up to 400µJ
* **Repetition Rates:** Single-shot to MHz
* **Beam Quality:** TEM00 / M² < 1.3

### neoMOS 10ps:

This picosecond laser series combines the reliability and low maintenance of state of the art
picosecond oscillators with a solid-state amplifier. The ultra-compact laser head has the smallest
footprint currently available, enabling easy system integration. High stability and long lifetime
are provided by design for 27/7 industrial use.
* **Pulse duration:** < 10ps
* **Output Power:** Up to 50W
* **Pulse Energy:** Up to 250µJ
* **Repetition Rates:** Single-shot to 40MHz
* **Beam Quality:** TEM00 / M² < 1.3

### neoMOS 70ps:

This picosecond laser series combines the reliability and low maintenance of a state of the art
picosecond laser diode with a solid-state amplifier. Customized combinations with different output
powers and flexible repetition rates are integrated into an ultra-compact laser head, enabling easy
system integration. High stability and long lifetime are provided by design for 24/7 industrial use.
* **Pulse duration:** 70ps
* **Output Power:** 15W
* **Pulse Energy:** Up to 250µJ
* **Repetition Rates:** Single-shot to 80MHz
* **FlexPulse Technologies**
* **Beam Quality:** TEM00 / M² < 1.3

## Pulsed Lasers FAQs

What is a Pulsed Laser?
**What is a Pulsed Laser?**

A [pulsed laser][139] is any laser that does not emit a continuous-wave (CW) laser beam. Instead,
they emit light pulses at some duration with some period of ‘off’ time between pulses and a
frequency measured in cycles per second (Hz). There are several different methods for pulse
generation, including passive and active q-switching and mode-locking. Pulsed lasers store energy
and release it in these pulses or energy packets. This pulsing can be very beneficial, for example,
when machining certain materials or features. The pulse can rapidly deliver the stored energy, with
downtime in between, preventing too much heat from building up in the material. If you would like to
read more about q-switches and the pros and cons of passive vs active q-switches, check out this
blog “[The Advantages and Disadvantages of Passive vs Active Q-Switching][140],” or check out our
[Overview of Pulsed Lasers][141] section on our Lasers 101 Page!

## Pulsed Lasers FAQs

What is a Pulsed Laser?
**What is a Pulsed Laser?**

A [pulsed laser][128] is any laser that does not emit a continuous-wave (CW) laser beam. Instead,
they emit light pulses at some duration with some period of ‘off’ time between pulses and a
frequency measured in cycles per second (Hz). There are several different methods for pulse
generation, including passive and active q-switching and mode-locking. Pulsed lasers store energy
and release it in these pulses or energy packets. This pulsing can be very beneficial, for example,
when machining certain materials or features. The pulse can rapidly deliver the stored energy, with
downtime in between, preventing too much heat from building up in the material. If you would like to
read more about q-switches and the pros and cons of passive vs active q-switches, check out this
blog “[The Advantages and Disadvantages of Passive vs Active Q-Switching][129],” or check out our
[Overview of Pulsed Lasers][130] section on our Lasers 101 Page!

What is the best laser for LIDAR?
**What is the best laser for LIDAR?**

There are actually numerous laser types that work well for various [LIDAR][131] and [3D
Scanning][132] applications. The answer comes down to what you want to measure or map. If your
target is stationary, and distance is the only necessary measurement, short-pulsed lasers, with
pulse durations of a few nanoseconds (even <1ns) and high pulse energy are what you’re looking for.
This is also accurate for 3D scanning applications (given a stationary, albeit a much closer
target), but select applications can also benefit from frequency-modulated, single-frequency
(narrow-linewidth) fiber lasers. If your target is moving, and speed is the critical measurement,
you need a single-frequency laser to ensure accurate measurement of the Doppler shift. If you want
to learn more about the various forms of LIDAR and the critical laser source requirements, check out
our [LIDAR][133] page for a list of detailed articles, as well as all the LIDAR laser source
products we offer. Get more information from our Lasers 101, Blogs, Whitepapers, FAQs, and Press
Release pages in our [Knowledge Center][134]!

## CW Lasers FAQs

How do I align my optical system?
**How do I align my optical system?**

Laser alignment can be a challenging task, but aligning a laser beam doesn’t have to be as
complicated as it might seem with the right optical alignment tools and proper laser alignment
techniques. Multiple optical alignment techniques have been developed over the years, utilized by
technicians and engineers to simplify the alignment process. With the development of these universal
laser beam alignment methods, along with some laser alignment tips and tricks, you don’t need to be
a laser expert to perform your alignments with relative ease, ensuring your laser beam path is right
where you want it to be and your beam is on target every time. Read our article, titled “[Laser
Alignment: HeNe Lasers, Methods, and Helpful Tips][108]” to get the knowledge and advice you need
for proper optical beam path alignment utilizing [HeNe Lasers][109]. Get more information from our
Lasers 101, Blogs, Whitepapers, FAQs, and Press Release pages in our [Knowledge Center][110]!

Should I choose multimode or single-mode for Raman spectroscopy?
**Should I choose multimode or single-mode for Raman spectroscopy?**

On the surface, this seems like a simple question since [Raman][111] is a nonlinear optical effect
and therefore the tighter the beam can be focused the higher the conversion efficiency. Seemingly a
single-mode laser would be preferable, but in practice there are other factors that can complicate
the situation. The first question you should ask yourself when considering which type of laser to
choose is whether you are doing microscopy or bulk sampling. If the answer to that question is
microscopy, then you immediately should go with a single mode laser. Since the goal of any
microscopy system is to produce the highest resolution image possible, the number one consideration
should be how tightly can the laser beam be focused down. However, there are several other
considerations when choosing between multimode and single-mode. Learn which is best for you in this
article: “[Multimode vs Single-Mode Lasers for Raman Spectroscopy][112].” Get more information from
our Lasers 101, Blogs, Whitepapers, FAQs, and Press Release pages in our [Knowledge Center][113]!

What is a CW Laser?
**What is a CW Laser?**

A [CW or continuous-wave laser][114] is any laser with a continuous flow of pump energy. It emits a
constant stream of radiation, as opposed to a q-switched or mode-locked pulsed laser with a pulsed
output beam. A laser is typically defined as having a pulse width greater than 250 ms. The first CW
laser was a helium-neon (HeNe) gas laser, developed in 1960, which you can read more about in this
blog “[HeNe Lasers: Bright Past, Brighter Future][115].” If you want to read more about the types of
CW Lasers we offer, check out the [Overview of CW Lasers][116] section on our Lasers 101 Page!

What is the best laser for optical surface flatness testing?
**What is the best laser for optical surface flatness testing?**

It is essential that the laser exhibit a high level of spectral stability, ensuring that any changes
in the interference pattern are caused by features in the sample and not originating from the laser
beam. In addition to spectral stability, high beam pointing stability ensures consistent
measurements by mitigating any beam position drift concerning the position of the sample. Lasers
with longer coherence lengths, and subsequently narrower linewidths, play an important role in
determining the resolution of the measurement, as well as consideration of the wavelength used.
Exhibiting both single longitudinal mode and single spatial mode has excellent benefits. Get more
information from our Lasers 101, Blogs, Whitepapers, FAQs, and Press Release pages in our [Knowledge
Center][117]!

What type of laser is best for Doppler LIDAR?
**What type of laser is best for Doppler LIDAR?**

Various LIDAR signal methods for measuring velocity have one critical requirement in common, the
need for precise control over laser frequency. While a wide variety of single-frequency lasers have
been used in Doppler LIDAR research, the industry as a whole has adopted [single-frequency fiber
lasers][118] as the ideal light source. Fiber lasers have several advantages over traditional DPSS
lasers, all of which derive from the geometry of the fiber optic itself, namely the innate ability
to have an extremely long single-mode optical cavity. This geometry allows for the production of
either extremely high-power, single-mode lasers producing unprecedented brightness, or extremely
narrow band lasers, with near perfect single-frequency output. If you want to learn more about
Doppler LIDAR, the critical considerations involved, and ideal laser sources, check out this
whitepaper: “[Single-Frequency Fiber Lasers for Doppler LIDAR][119].” Get more information from our
Lasers 101, Blogs, Whitepapers, FAQs, and Press Release pages in our [Knowledge Center][120]!

##### Check out this white paper, authored by one of our successful customers, titled:

**“Optoacoustic Brain Stimulation at Submillimeter Spatial Precision”**

[ Read the Article!][92]

**Summary: **Utilizing a 1030nm One Series laser from Bright Solutions, we report spatially confined
optoacoustic neural stimulation through a miniaturized Fiber-Optoacoustic Converter (FOC). The FOC
has a diameter of 600µm and generates omnidirectional ultrasound wave locally at the fiber tip
through the optoacoustic effect. We show that the acoustic wave generated by FOC can directly
activate individual cultured neurons and generate intracellular Ca^2 transients. The FOC activates
neurons within a radius of 500µm around the fiber tip, delivering superior spatial resolution over
conventional piezo-based low-frequency transducers. Finally, we demonstrate direct and spatially
confined neural stimulation of mouse brain and modulation of motor activity in vivo.

What is a Pulsed Laser?
**What is a Pulsed Laser?**

A [pulsed laser][132] is any laser that does not emit a continuous-wave (CW) laser beam. Instead,
they emit light pulses at some duration with some period of ‘off’ time between pulses and a
frequency measured in cycles per second (Hz). There are several different methods for pulse
generation, including passive and active q-switching and mode-locking. Pulsed lasers store energy
and release it in these pulses or energy packets. This pulsing can be very beneficial, for example,
when machining certain materials or features. The pulse can rapidly deliver the stored energy, with
downtime in between, preventing too much heat from building up in the material. If you would like to

The **FL CW/CW Modulated Series** is a versatile, high-performance line of continuous-wave (CW)
fiber lasers manufactured to Telcordia standards. This series is ideal for various industrial and
scientific applications, offering power outputs up to 100W at 1μm, 30W at 1.5μm, and 40W at 2μm.
Available in both OEM and turnkey configurations, the series provides users with options like narrow
linewidth single-frequency outputs, polarization-maintaining (PM) fibers, C and L-band broadband
sources, and high-speed modulation and triggering. The lasers’ flexible, modular design ensures easy
integration into diverse environments, with the ability to customize the system to meet specific
application requirements, such as material processing, optical metrology, and sensing.

### **1, 1.5, 2 µm CW & CW Modulated Fiber Lasers – Configuration Examples**

The 1um, 1.5um, and 2um CW/CW modulated fiber lasers provide high-power, continuous-wave outputs
with power tunability ranging from 10%-100%. These lasers are available in both standard and
polarization-maintaining (PM) fiber options and come equipped with either FC/APC fiber connectors or
other option, including collimating lenses. Our SWIR CW fiber lasers deliver exceptional beam
quality, producing a perfect TEM00 output, and offer options for high-speed modulation and
triggering for applications requiring precise control. These lasers are suitable for a wide range of
industrial and scientific applications, including material processing, optical metrology, and
sensing. Power outputs range from 2W to 100W, with multiple wavelength configurations across the
1μm, 1.5μm, and 2μm ranges to fit diverse application needs.

compact design makes it ideal for systems where space and reliability are critical, providing
high-quality, customizable laser solutions for the most demanding environments.

Whether it’s the CPFL group with its Telcom-grade compact pulsed lasers for long-range LIDAR and
eye-safe operations, or the HFL group, offering high-energy, wavelength-stabilized, Q-switched
lasers for applications like LiDAR and 3D scanning, the FL-P series ensures flexibility across a
wide spectrum of pulse widths, repetition rates, and center wavelengths. With pulse energies up to
150µJ, pulse repetition rates in the MHz range, and perfect TEM00 beam quality, these lasers are
built to meet the exacting demands of modern applications.

The REP series includes high-performance single-mode Fabry-Perot laser diodes in wavelengths from
760nm through 2350nm. These laser diodes are designed to address challenges in industries like Gas
Sensing, LIDAR, Spectroscopy, and Telecom. The REP series includes high-power options, at the most
popular wavelengths, and provides customizable units with multiple packaging options, including the
Fiber coupled 14-pin butterfly, TO39 (w/TEC), TO56, and DX1 Modules.

We are committed to finding the perfect laser for your application by matching our expertise in
laser design with diverse customer requirements, from research to volume production. Our
high-performance laser diodes enable our customers to solve problems in various industries, with
customizable units that can be tailored to specific needs. Whether you require high power or narrow
linewidth options, we offer a range of products at the most popular NIR and SWIR wavelengths to meet
your needs. You can trust in our industry-leading performance, consistent production, and
integration capability to provide you with your ideal laser solution.

### Package Options

Here at RPMC Lasers, we offer a wide range of package configurations to meet your application,
operating environment, and integration needs. The table below provides you with a detailed list of
all of the different packaging configurations available.

#### 14-pin Butterfly Module

The 14-pin butterfly package is designed with stability and ease of use in mind. Tested to Telcordia
standards, it is the ideal package for thermal stability and fiber-coupled integration.

##### Key features
* Integral TEC
* PM/SMF Coupled with FC/APC
* Built-in Optical Isolator

#### TO-39 with TEC

The TO-39 incorporates an internal TEC for accurate wavelength control. We have worked with
industrial partners to design a free space package specifically for the gas sensing industry.

##### Key features
* Integral TEC
* Angled AR Coated Window
* Free-space Design

#### TO-56

The TO-56 package is tested to Telcordia standard and is RoHS qualified. Available with either a
flat window or a ball lens and is typically used for high-volume communications applications.

##### Key features
* Free-space Design
* Hermetically Sealed
* Flat Window or 1.5 mm Ball Lens

#### High-speed 7-pin Butterfly

The high-speed and pulsing capabilities of DM and FP laser diodes can be fully exploited using the
high-speed 7-pin butterfly, which incorporates a K-connector for modulation up to 10 GHz.

##### Key features
* K-connector for High-speed Modulation
* PM/SMF Coupled with FC/APC
* Built-in Optical Isolator

#### DX-1 Module

The DX-1 incorporates the butterfly module with an integrated current driver and TEC controller.
Designed for ease of operation, it is the ideal platform for high-stability gas detection or remote
sensing.

##### Key features
* Integral Driver and TEC Controller
* PM/SMF Coupled with FC/APC
* Built-in Optical Isolator
* Powered by 5 V DC Source

The JOLD-Open Heatsinks Series offers industry-leading, reliable, and cost-effective high-power
free-space single-laser-bar packages based on passively or actively cooled heat sinks in the
760-1070 nm range. Our proprietary heat sink and assembly technology, paired with our focus on
advanced optical pumping and direct-diode-laser technology, results in diode lasers with unmatched
performance including optical output power, electro-optical (EO) efficiency, and lifetime. This
series offers options from 792 nm up to 1035 nm, and average output powers up to 300 W CW with
passive cooling.

**Your OEM Laser Diode Solution Awaits!**

[ Tell us what you need!][84]

### Many configuration options available:
* **Wavelength:** Options from 760-1070 nm
* **Optical output power:** up to 300 W
* **Operating mode:** CW or QCW

### Cooling Options:
* **Passively cooled** heat sinks, i.e. single-bar packages which conductively spread and transfer
dissipated power to a baseplate before waste heat is ultimately removed, e.g. via tap water
cooling of the baseplate
* **Actively cooled** heat sinks i.e. single-bar packages which are directly cooled with water in
order to convectively remove the heat directly from the heat sink
* *Active cooling allows for a smaller and narrower heat sink design which still make this heat
sink technology an attractive building-block for densely packed horizontal arrays serving e.g.
side-pumping applications*

### Packaging Options:

While still supplying industry standard heat sink designs (CS, CT) and established assembly
technologies based on In or AuSn soldering, Jenoptik is leveraging **our proprietary, cutting-edge
heat sinking and die attach technologies** within our double-side passively cooled packages CN, LS
and LK in order to serve most advanced optical pumping schemes and direct-diode-laser (DDL)
technology.

Close cooperation between our in-house laser bar fab and our laser assembly site ensures a laser bar
tailored to the specific heat sink technology, operating parameters, and application specific needs.

### **Lensing Options: **
* **Beam collimation** using microlenses.
* **Beam shaping** using diffractive optical elements (DOE).

## Pulsed Lasers FAQs

What is a Pulsed Laser?
**What is a Pulsed Laser?**

A [pulsed laser][117] is any laser that does not emit a continuous-wave (CW) laser beam. Instead,
they emit light pulses at some duration with some period of ‘off’ time between pulses and a
frequency measured in cycles per second (Hz). There are several different methods for pulse
generation, including passive and active q-switching and mode-locking. Pulsed lasers store energy
and release it in these pulses or energy packets. This pulsing can be very beneficial, for example,
when machining certain materials or features. The pulse can rapidly deliver the stored energy, with
downtime in between, preventing too much heat from building up in the material. If you would like to
read more about q-switches and the pros and cons of passive vs active q-switches, check out this
blog “[The Advantages and Disadvantages of Passive vs Active Q-Switching][118],” or check out our
[Overview of Pulsed Lasers][119] section on our Lasers 101 Page!

**Jasper X1: Amplified fiber laser system with integrated robust, Truly All-Fiber femtosecond
oscillator.**

The Jasper X1 is a high-performance femtosecond laser system designed for maximum flexibility and
precision in demanding applications like precision materials processing, micromachining, and
advanced glass cutting & processing, providing up to 60 W average power and up to 200 µJ pulses. It
features extended burst lengths with flexible envelope adjustment (Custom Envelope Burst – CEB)
supporting bursts up to 80 pulses, along with tunable pulse durations from less than 270 fs up to 20
ps. This allows for precise process optimization tailored to a wide range of materials and
applications.

With Advanced Pulse-on-Demand (APoD) and nanosecond-level jitter, Jasper X1 delivers exceptional
pulse timing precision—ideal for enhancing edge definition, corner processing, and maximized duty
cycles. Built as a robust, all-fiber, SESAM-free system, Jasper X1 ensures consistent performance,
long-term stability, and exceptional lifetime, with true maintenance-free 24/7 operation. The Jasper
Series offers superior beam quality thanks to its all-fiber optical design, immediate reaction to
external trigger signals providing 100-fold accuracy improvement, and a standard 5-year warranty on
the oscillator with 2 years on the complete laser.

solutions based on a standard technology. The series includes:

envelope burst feature

jitter and specialized triggering architecture

Each model provides a fast warm-up time, long-term stability, and hands-free operation. The JX30-100

## Pulsed Lasers FAQs

What is a Pulsed Laser?
**What is a Pulsed Laser?**

A [pulsed laser][138] is any laser that does not emit a continuous-wave (CW) laser beam. Instead,
they emit light pulses at some duration with some period of ‘off’ time between pulses and a
frequency measured in cycles per second (Hz). There are several different methods for pulse
generation, including passive and active q-switching and mode-locking. Pulsed lasers store energy
and release it in these pulses or energy packets. This pulsing can be very beneficial, for example,
when machining certain materials or features. The pulse can rapidly deliver the stored energy, with
downtime in between, preventing too much heat from building up in the material. If you would like to
read more about q-switches and the pros and cons of passive vs active q-switches, check out this
blog “[The Advantages and Disadvantages of Passive vs Active Q-Switching][139],” or check out our
[Overview of Pulsed Lasers][140] section on our Lasers 101 Page!

## Pulsed Lasers FAQs

What is a Pulsed Laser?
**What is a Pulsed Laser?**

A [pulsed laser][135] is any laser that does not emit a continuous-wave (CW) laser beam. Instead,
they emit light pulses at some duration with some period of ‘off’ time between pulses and a
frequency measured in cycles per second (Hz). There are several different methods for pulse
generation, including passive and active q-switching and mode-locking. Pulsed lasers store energy
and release it in these pulses or energy packets. This pulsing can be very beneficial, for example,
when machining certain materials or features. The pulse can rapidly deliver the stored energy, with
downtime in between, preventing too much heat from building up in the material. If you would like to
read more about q-switches and the pros and cons of passive vs active q-switches, check out this
blog “[The Advantages and Disadvantages of Passive vs Active Q-Switching][136],” or check out our
[Overview of Pulsed Lasers][137] section on our Lasers 101 Page!

What is the best laser for LIDAR?
**What is the best laser for LIDAR?**

There are actually numerous laser types that work well for various [LIDAR][138] and [3D
Scanning][139] applications. The answer comes down to what you want to measure or map. If your
target is stationary, and distance is the only necessary measurement, short-pulsed lasers, with
pulse durations of a few nanoseconds (even <1ns) and high pulse energy are what you’re looking for.
This is also accurate for 3D scanning applications (given a stationary, albeit a much closer
target), but select applications can also benefit from frequency-modulated, single-frequency
(narrow-linewidth) fiber lasers. If your target is moving, and speed is the critical measurement,
you need a single-frequency laser to ensure accurate measurement of the Doppler shift. If you want
to learn more about the various forms of LIDAR and the critical laser source requirements, check out
our [LIDAR][140] page for a list of detailed articles, as well as all the LIDAR laser source
products we offer. Get more information from our Lasers 101, Blogs, Whitepapers, FAQs, and Press
Release pages in our [Knowledge Center][141]!

What is the best laser for tattoo removal?
**What is the best laser for tattoo removal?**

The best laser for tattoo removal depends on factors like wavelength versatility, pulse duration,
and energy output to effectively target various ink colors while minimizing skin damage. Q-switched
or ultrafast lasers with pulse durations of 100 ps to 10 ns and a fluence of ~10 J/cm² are ideal for
fragmenting ink via selective photothermolysis. For example, the [Lampo][142] 266-1064 nm offers
multiple wavelengths (266 nm, 532 nm, 1064 nm) for multi-color tattoos, while the [Nimbus][143]
770-1064 nm provides customizable sub-nanosecond pulses for precision. The [Quantas-Q1][144]
delivers high pulse energy (up to 32 mJ at 1064 nm) for efficient treatments.

For more details on pulsed lasers for tattoo removal applications, see our blog, “[Choosing the
Right Laser for Tattoo Removal: Key Considerations][145]‘! Get more information from our Lasers 101,
Blogs, Whitepapers, and FAQ pages in our [Knowledge Center][146]!

**What is the best laser for LIDAR?**

There are actually numerous laser types that work well for various [LIDAR][138] and [3D
Scanning][139] applications. The answer comes down to what you want to measure or map. If your
target is stationary, and distance is the only necessary measurement, short-pulsed lasers, with
pulse durations of a few nanoseconds (even <1ns) and high pulse energy are what you’re looking for.
This is also accurate for 3D scanning applications (given a stationary, albeit a much closer
target), but select applications can also benefit from frequency-modulated, single-frequency
(narrow-linewidth) fiber lasers. If your target is moving, and speed is the critical measurement,
you need a single-frequency laser to ensure accurate measurement of the Doppler shift. If you want
to learn more about the various forms of LIDAR and the critical laser source requirements, check out
our [LIDAR][140] page for a list of detailed articles, as well as all the LIDAR laser source
products we offer. Get more information from our Lasers 101, Blogs, Whitepapers, FAQs, and Press
Release pages in our [Knowledge Center][141]!

What is the best laser for tattoo removal?
**What is the best laser for tattoo removal?**

The best laser for tattoo removal depends on factors like wavelength versatility, pulse duration,
and energy output to effectively target various ink colors while minimizing skin damage. Q-switched
or ultrafast lasers with pulse durations of 100 ps to 10 ns and a fluence of ~10 J/cm² are ideal for
fragmenting ink via selective photothermolysis. For example, the [Lampo][142] 266-1064 nm offers
multiple wavelengths (266 nm, 532 nm, 1064 nm) for multi-color tattoos, while the [Nimbus][143]
770-1064 nm provides customizable sub-nanosecond pulses for precision. The [Quantas-Q1][144]
delivers high pulse energy (up to 32 mJ at 1064 nm) for efficient treatments.

For more details on pulsed lasers for tattoo removal applications, see our blog, “[Choosing the
Right Laser for Tattoo Removal: Key Considerations][145]‘! Get more information from our Lasers 101,
Blogs, Whitepapers, and FAQ pages in our [Knowledge Center][146]!

What is a Pulsed Laser?
**What is a Pulsed Laser?**

A [pulsed laser][138] is any laser that does not emit a continuous-wave (CW) laser beam. Instead,
they emit light pulses at some duration with some period of ‘off’ time between pulses and a
frequency measured in cycles per second (Hz). There are several different methods for pulse
generation, including passive and active q-switching and mode-locking. Pulsed lasers store energy
and release it in these pulses or energy packets. This pulsing can be very beneficial, for example,
when machining certain materials or features. The pulse can rapidly deliver the stored energy, with
downtime in between, preventing too much heat from building up in the material. If you would like to
read more about q-switches and the pros and cons of passive vs active q-switches, check out this
blog “[The Advantages and Disadvantages of Passive vs Active Q-Switching][139],” or check out our
[Overview of Pulsed Lasers][140] section on our Lasers 101 Page!

# Sonic Laser Tech

## About Us

[About Sonic Laser]

As the official Indian distributor of the renowned Raycus brand, Sonic Laser Tech is at the
forefront of delivering advanced laser intelligent equipment and comprehensive technical services.
We specialize in high-performance solutions for laser cutting and laser welding, tailored to meet
the evolving needs of modern industries.

Our commitment to excellence is reflected in every aspect of our work. Backed by a team of seasoned
professionals with deep industry expertise, we ensure our clients receive reliable, efficient, and
innovative support. At Sonic Laser Tech, we don’t just provide equipment — we deliver end-to-end
solutions that empower businesses to achieve precision, productivity, and progress.
* #### [ Robust Technical Support
  #### Why choose us ][5]

We specialize in providing comprehensive pre-sales and after-sales support for Raycus brand lasers,
ensuring your equipment performs at its best throughout its lifecycle. From expert guidance during
the selection process to reliable maintenance and troubleshooting after installation, our team is
committed to keeping your laser systems in optimal condition.
* #### [ Efficient Logistics Services
  #### Why choose us ][6]

With a robust and expansive logistics network throughout Europe, we guarantee fast delivery,
reliable service, and prompt responses tailored to your business needs. Whether it's urgent
shipments or routine deliveries, our streamlined operations ensure your goods arrive on time, every
time.
* #### [ Flexible Leasing Solutions
  #### Why choose us ][7]

We offer tailored leasing and financing services designed to meet your unique operational needs.
Whether you're looking to optimize cash flow, upgrade equipment, or expand your capabilities, our
flexible solutions help you stay agile and financially efficient.

## Our Powerful Services

[48x48x1]

##### [Laser Consulting][8]

Welcome to Sonic Laser Tech, your trusted partner in laser consulting. With years of experience and
a team of industry experts, Sonic Laser Tech is committed to providing comprehensive solutions for
laser technology to our customers. We provide expert advice on Raycus fiber lasers, laser services,
and laser applications.

[48x48x2]

##### [Laser Repair][9]

If your Raycus fiber laser is experiencing issues or requires maintenance, our expert technicians
are here to help. With extensive experience and specialized knowledge, we diagnose and repair a wide
range of problems efficiently—ensuring your machine is back up and running with minimal downtime.

[48x48x3]

##### [Raycus Customer Center][10]

With offices in Surat and Vadodara, Gujarat, India, we are strategically positioned to serve the
growing demand for high-performance fiber laser technology across the Indian market.

## Applications

[750x500x1]

#### Laser Cutting

Laser cutting is an advanced manufacturing process that employs a high-powered, focused laser beam
to precisely cut through various materials. The laser heats the material to the point where it
melts, burns, vaporizes, or is expelled by a jet of gas, resulting in a clean and accurate edge.
This technique is widely used in industrial applications for cutting metals, plastics, wood, and
composite materials due to its speed, precision, and versatility.

[Read More][11]
[750x500x2]

#### Laser Welding

Laser welding is an advanced technique used to join materials—typically metals or thermoplastics—by
directing a concentrated laser beam at the joint. The high energy density of the focused beam
enables precise control over heat input, resulting in strong, high-quality welds. This method is
valued for its speed, accuracy, and minimal thermal distortion, making it ideal for applications
requiring fine detail and clean finishes.

[Read More][12]

relevant_companies.polished_summary: Thales Group is a global leader in advanced technologies, specializing in aerospace, defense, transportation, and security solutions. The company develops innovative products and services that enhance safety and efficiency across various sectors, catering to both governmental and commercial markets. With a commitment to delivering cutting-edge solutions, Thales Group plays a pivotal role in shaping the future of critical infrastructure and defense systems.
relevant_companies.audit_reasoning: The company is a recognized manufacturer of high energy laser systems, which aligns directly with the specified market scope of high energy laser systems and directed energy weapons.

relevant_companies.company_summary: The Boeing Company is a leading aerospace manufacturer that designs and produces a comprehensive range of commercial and defense aircraft, space systems, and services. With a focus on innovation and safety, Boeing delivers advanced solutions such as the 737 MAX, 777X, and military systems that enhance operational capabilities for customers in the aviation, defense, and space sectors. The company is committed to connecting people and economies while advancing global security through its cutting-edge technologies and services.

Proyecto de personalización privado grupal.
Solicitud
Depilación Láser
La depilación láser es un procedimiento médico que utiliza un haz de luz concentrado (láser) para
eliminar el vello no deseado de forma segura y eficaz. Pero muchas máquinas de depilación se
estropean después de un uso prolongado. La razón suele ser que la pila de láser de diodo dentro del
mango está quemada.
[leer más][116]
Láser Industrial
Los láseres se utilizan en la industria en una gran variedad de aplicaciones, como revestimiento
láser, limpieza láser y procesamiento de materiales. BrandNew proporciona módulos láser de
acoplamiento de fibra y módulos de fibra de longitud de onda estabilizada con tecnología avanzada de
acoplamiento de fibra y conformación óptica.

Depilación Láser
La depilación láser es un procedimiento médico que utiliza un haz de luz concentrado (láser) para
eliminar el vello no deseado de forma segura y eficaz. Pero muchas máquinas de depilación se
estropean después de un uso prolongado. La razón suele ser que la pila de láser de diodo dentro del
mango está quemada.

acoplamiento de fibra y módulos de fibra de longitud de onda estabilizada con tecnología avanzada de
acoplamiento de fibra y conformación óptica.

non-metals, PCBs, ICs, and semiconductor wafers as well as a wide range of other materials. Our

with the lowest power consumption, fastest processing speed, highest reliability and superior safety
performance.We also provide customers with customization services to support laser marking of any
pattern and for nearly any material, along with tailor-made mass production solutions that deliver
high efficiency and cost-effectiveness.

# Laser Welding Equipment

Han’s Laser’s self-developed high-tech laser welding machines adopt advanced optoelectronic control
systems, rational heat dissipation layout and optimized optical path output solutions. Featuring
high automation and integration, our laser welding machines support semi-automatic and fully
automatic loading and unloading, delivering high welding efficiency and one-step forming with
aesthetic weld seams, superior tightness and minimal deformation.

# Optical Fiber & Pump Source

Pump sources are applied to Fiber Lasers, Solid-state Lasers, Direct Diode Lasers and other laser
types. They optically excite laser working medium, pump active particles from ground state to high
energy level to achieve population inversion and realize laser output. Special optical fibers
satisfy requirements of low, medium and high-power Fiber Lasers with high beam quality. Special
Optical Fiber Preform is mainly used to fabricate double-clad single-mode gain fiber, double-clad
high-energy gain fiber, high-power gain fiber and matched transmission fiber for fiber lasers.

meet diverse application demands. Our self-developed laser products cover CO₂ Laser, CW Fiber Laser,
Pulsed Fiber Laser, Welding Laser, UV & Ultrafast Lasers, Femtosecond and Sub-nanosecond Lasers.

# New Energy Lithium-ion Battery

# New Energy Lithium-ion Battery

[Applications][186] [New Energy Lithium-ion Battery][187]

## Intelligent Manufacturing Solutions for Lithium-ion Batteries

Lithium-ion batteries, as eco-friendly and high-efficiency energy storage devices, are seeing
surging market demand.
Han's Laser has completed the product layout of integrated intelligent equipment for the front-end
processes of lithium-ion battery production, with outstanding process innovations and efficiency
improvements. Our product portfolio includes integrated machines such as calendering & slitting
all-in-one machines, laser die-cutting & slitting all-in-one machines, laser die-cutting & winding
all-in-one machines, and cutting & stacking all-in-one machines.
We also offer high-performance standalone equipment for standard front-end production processes,
including slitting machines, winding machines and stacking machines.
Our solutions have been adopted by numerous well-known enterprises, helping them achieve remarkable
improvements in production efficiency and product quality, and have earned wide recognition across
the market.

Contact Us

## Intelligent Manufacturing Solutions for ESS Lithium-ion Batteries

As a major development model for new energy storage, lithium-ion battery energy storage is currently
in a period of rapid expansion.
Han's Laser delivers comprehensive process solutions for the production of various battery
components, covering complete power battery production lines, cell sealing (side welding, top
welding) and plug sealing, flexible busbar connections, battery module welding, as well as welding
for explosion-proof valves, explosion-proof covers, throttle valves, current collectors and terminal
posts. Our product portfolio also includes plug sealing, cleaning for modules, cells and separators,
cell marking and tab cutting. We also provide turnkey solutions for complete power battery
production lines.
Tailored to clients' requirements, our solutions seamlessly connect upstream and downstream
processes. Leveraging intelligent manufacturing technologies, we support the efficient, high-quality
and sustainable development of energy storage lithium-ion batteries.

Contact Us

## Intelligent Manufacturing Solutions for Consumer Lithium-ion Batteries

Driven by rising demand for smartphones, wearable devices, drones, service robots and other
products, consumer batteries have become a major growth driver in the consumer lithium battery
market.
Pouch cells are liquid lithium-ion batteries encapsulated with a polymer casing and packaged with
aluminum-plastic composite films, which effectively reduces electrolyte leakage. In the event of
potential safety hazards, pouch cells only swell and rupture, unlike metal-cased batteries that may
explode due to excessive internal pressure. Featuring a stacked internal structure, pouch cells are
lightweight.
Han's Laser supplies automated production equipment for pouch cells. Composed of independent modular
units, the equipment can be customized to meet customers' process requirements, featuring strong
compatibility, high automation and proven process performance.

Contact Us

## Intelligent Manufacturing Solutions for Hydrogen Fuel Cells

Battery quality directly determines the performance of new energy vehicles, so extremely high
precision is required throughout its manufacturing processes. As an advanced photonic manufacturing
tool, laser technology features high efficiency, superior precision, great flexibility, reliable
stability, low material consumption, high automation and safety. It is widely adopted in cutting,
cleaning, welding, marking and other processes for power lithium-ion battery components.
Leveraging extensive experience and robust technical expertise in lithium battery manufacturing,
Han's Laser has launched intelligent manufacturing solutions for hydrogen fuel cells to meet market
demands for high-quality, high-efficiency, eco-friendly and sustainable hydrogen fuel cells.

## Laser Scribing & Soldering Process for PV Modules

Fully automatic laser scribing & breaking machines are applied to automated production of
high-efficiency PV modules. Scribed modules reduce string current and resistance loss, thus boosting

# Electronic Information Industry

[Applications][186] [Electronic Information Industry][187]

## Laser Welding for Consumer Electronics

Laser welding is widely used in the precision processing of various consumer electronic functional
components such as motors, VCMs, phone shrapnels, cameras, studs, heat sinks, fingerprint modules,
connectors and carrier tapes, covering a broad range of application scenarios.
Featuring non-contact operation, high precision and great flexibility, laser welding enables
ultra-fine micro-processing for consumer electronic products, and fully meets the requirements of 3C
products for high speed, high efficiency, stable performance, high reliability and attractive
appearance.
The advantages of laser welding solutions for consumer electronics include high precision, high
efficiency, high yield rate, high automation level, aesthetic finish, environmental friendliness,
clean operation and strong versatility.

Contact Us

## Flexible Material Processing

The laser processing solution for flexible materials is a technical solution that processes
materials via interaction between laser beams and workpieces, covering laser cutting, laser marking
and laser welding.
Its strengths include high precision, high efficiency, high automation and zero thermal effect.
This technology is applicable to a wide range of materials, such as metals, non-metals and composite
materials. Widely adopted in the manufacturing sector, it serves multiple fields including
electronics, automotive, medical, construction and furniture.
It delivers precision cutting, grooving and other processes for PCBA, FPCA, LCP, SIP packaged chips,
rigid-flex boards, cover films, polarizers, PI films, PET films, metal foils and more.

Contact Us

## Brittle Material Processing

Laser processing solutions for brittle materials mainly include laser cutting and laser welding.
The advantages are high precision, high efficiency, high automation, zero thermal effect,
environmental friendliness and capability of thin sheet cutting.
This technology is applicable to various materials such as metals, non-metals and composite
materials.

## Laser Welding & Automation Solutions for Kitchenware and Sanitary Ware

Han's Laser provides professional laser welding and automation solutions for the kitchenware and
sanitary ware industry, covering the following key areas:
1. Laser Welding for Kitchen & Sanitary Hardware Parts
Han's Laser offers a full range of laser welding equipment to deliver high-efficiency and
high-precision welding for hardware parts made of stainless steel, aluminum alloy, copper, iron and
other materials. Featuring high precision, high productivity and excellent uniformity, our welding
equipment ensures stable and consistent welding quality.

2. Automated Production Lines for Kitchenware & Sanitary Ware
We have developed multiple automated production line solutions tailored for this industry, including
digital modules, welding robots, intelligent cutting machines and multi-arm rotary resistance
welders. These solutions enable fully automatic production from raw materials to finished products,
lifting overall productivity and product uniformity.

3. Welding Quality Control for Kitchenware & Sanitary Ware
With extensive industry experience, Han's Laser has launched diverse quality control solutions such
as in-line inspection, manual inspection and machine vision inspection. They monitor key welding
indicators in real time, including penetration depth, porosity and heat input, to sustain reliable
and uniform welding performance.

4. Welding for Tableware & Drinkware
Our laser welding equipment is applicable to tableware and drinkware of stainless steel, aluminum
alloy, copper and more. The equipment boasts high precision, high efficiency and superior
consistency, guaranteeing steady and uniform welding quality.

## Laser Welding & Automation Solutions for Home Appliance Hardware

Han's Laser’s laser welding and automation solutions for home appliance hardware supply dedicated
laser welding equipment and automated production lines for automated manufacturing of home appliance
hardware. These solutions help boost productivity, cut production costs and ensure reliable product
quality.
Our laser welding machines are capable of processing various metals including stainless steel,
aluminum, copper and iron, suitable for welding a wide range of hardware products. We also deliver
customized automated production lines integrating multiple processes such as CNC shearing, bending,
dispensing and riveting, enabling high-efficiency, high-quality and highly automated production of
home appliance hardware.
